name: Kosovo
summary_text: Kosovo is workable for trans visitors — the Balkans' strongest legal framework on paper. The constitution (Art 24) bans discrimination based on sexual orientation; the 2015 Law on Protection from Discrimination covers gender identity; legal gender recognition is possible (medicalised); and the government attempted same-sex unions in 2024 as part of Council of Europe accession. Counterweights: implementation is inconsistent, political hate speech is common (2022 CSGD report: year marked by intolerance), and Pristina Pride proceeds under protection.

sources.title: Kosovo | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): progressive protections on paper with inconsistent implementation - constitutional ban on SO discrimination (Article 24); the 2015 Law on Protection from Discrimination covers gender identity; legal gender recognition possible but bureaucratically burdensome (the Blert Morina court ruling affirmed that requiring medical interventions is unconstitutional, but no self-determination-based procedure exists, forcing litigation); the constitution defines marriage neutrally but the Family Law restricts it to different-sex couples; PM Kurti's April 2024 civil-union announcement stalled.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (May 2024) covers Muslim-majority Kosovo considering same-sex unions amid fierce opposition.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Kosovo: PM Kurti said during Pride week he would 'do his utmost' to get the Civil Code adopted (2022 parliament had voted against same-sex-couple recognition amendments); a Justice Ministry working group was drafting a bill; CSGD's 2022 annual report found intolerance and hatred, with politicians' hate speech common during Civil Code debates; an artist received death threats over a painting; Kosovo Pride Week held with the motto 'I love you as you are!'.

sources.title: Kosovo turns its eye on Macedonian transgender rights - Prishtina Insight Prishtina Insight
sources.claim_summary: Prishtina Insight (Jan 2019): 'Kosovo turns its eye on Macedonian transgender rights' - the ECtHR ruling in X v FYROM (surgery requirement violates private-life rights) is watched closely by Blert Morina, whose own Constitutional Court case challenges Kosovo's refusal to change his name and gender marker; his lawyer Rina Kika: 'Macedonia's case could be a huge turning point for the future of the transgender community all over the Balkans.'

sources.title: Kosovo's parliament rejects new law recognising same-sex civil unions | Euronews
sources.claim_summary: Euronews (March 2022): Kosovo's parliament rejected the new law recognising same-sex civil unions (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: Pride Week kicks off in Prishtina - Prishtina Insight
sources.claim_summary: Prishtina Insight: 'Pride Week kicks off in Prishtina' - before the third annual Pride Parade (slogan 'Whomever your heart beats for'), CEL organised exhibitions, parties, conferences and discussions; the slogan is 'an appeal for tolerance, understanding and acceptance' and an invitation to declare LGBTI rights as basic human rights.

sources.title: bne IntelliNews - Kosovo’s new civil code opens the way for gay marriage
sources.claim_summary: IntelliNews: 'Kosovo's new Civil Code opens the way for gay marriage' - analysis of the Civil Code's gender-neutral marriage language and its implications (page largely navigation content at fetch time).
